theorem.statement:
For \(R\geq 4\) and \(c=(m,u,v,p,q)\in\mathcal C_R\), put \(N=N_c\) and define
\[
 k(c)=\min\left\{s\in\left\{0,\ldots,\left\lfloor m/2\right\rfloor\right\}:\binom ms\geq N\right\},
 \qquad
 c^\circ=\bigl(m,\mathbf 1_m,\mathbf 1_m,k(c),k(c)\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathbf 1_m=(1,\ldots,1)\).  Then this minimum exists, the map \(c\mapsto c^\circ\) realizes \(\mathsf{Purify}_R\), and
\[
 c^\circ\in\mathcal U_R,
 \qquad 2N_{c^\circ}\geq 2N_c,
 \qquad f_{c^\circ}(n_B,n_S)\geq f_c(n_B,n_S)
\]
simultaneously for all \(n_B,n_S\geq4R\).  Support equality holds if and only if \(N_c=\binom{m}{k(c)}\).  Phase-score equality at one, equivalently every, pair \(n_B,n_S\geq4R\) holds if and only if \(c\in\mathcal U_R\); in that case \(p=q\) and \(c^\circ\) equals \(c\) or its simultaneous complement.  If \(c\notin\mathcal U_R\), the phase-score inequality is strict throughout that quadrant.

Moreover, define
\[
 \mu_R=\min\left\{m\geq1:2\binom{m}{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\geq R\right\},
 \qquad
 \kappa_R=\min\left\{s\in\left\{0,\ldots,\left\lfloor\mu_R/2\right\rfloor\right\}:2\binom{\mu_R}{s}\geq R\right\}.
\]
Then the exact frontier is
\[
 \Phi_{n_B,n_S}(R)
 =2n_Bn_S-\mu_R(n_B+n_S)
   +\kappa_R^2+(\mu_R-\kappa_R)^2+\mu_R.
\]
All equality cases are the catalog-induced profiles of
\(c_R^\star=(\mu_R,\mathbf 1_{\mu_R},\mathbf 1_{\mu_R},\kappa_R,\kappa_R)\)
and its simultaneous complement, modulo a common block permutation; when the two entries coincide they represent one equality case.
theorem.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal F_c=\left\{J\subseteq[m]:
       \sum_{i\in J}u_i=p,
       \ \sum_{i\in J}v_i=q\right\}.
\]
By the definition of \(N_c\), this family has cardinality \(N=N_c\).  It is an antichain: if \(J\subsetneq J'\), positivity of every \(u_i\) gives
\(\sum_{i\in J}u_i<\sum_{i\in J'}u_i\), so both sets cannot lie in \(\mathcal F_c\).

We first prove the rank-layer fact needed below.  For each \(J\in\mathcal F_c\), exactly
\(|J|!(m-|J|)!\) permutations of \([m]\) have \(J\) as their first \(|J|\) elements.  For a fixed permutation, two distinct initial segments are nested, whereas \(\mathcal F_c\) is an antichain.  Hence the corresponding sets of permutations are disjoint, and double counting gives
\[
 \sum_{J\in\mathcal F_c}|J|!(m-|J|)!\leq m!,
 \qquad\text{or equivalently}\qquad
 \sum_{J\in\mathcal F_c}\binom m{|J|}^{-1}\leq1.                 \tag{1}
\]
If \(\binom m{|J|}<N\) held for every \(J\in\mathcal F_c\), the left side of (1) would be strictly larger than \(N/N=1\), a contradiction.  Thus there is a \(J_0\in\mathcal F_c\), of cardinality \(r\), such that \(\binom mr\geq N\).  The ratios
\[
 \frac{\binom m{s+1}}{\binom ms}=\frac{m-s}{s+1}
\]
show that the binomial coefficients increase up to the middle and are symmetric about it.  Consequently the defining set for \(k=k(c)\) is nonempty and
\[
 k\leq \min\{r,m-r\}.                                             \tag{2}
\]
Because \(2N_c\geq R\geq4\), one has \(N\geq2\), and (1) also implies \(m\geq2\).

For the unit tuple \(c^\circ\), a residual subset has both target sums equal to \(k\) exactly when it has cardinality \(k\).  Therefore
\[
 N_{c^\circ}=\binom mk\geq N_c.                                  \tag{3}
\]
Positivity of the original coordinates gives \(m\leq A\) and \(m\leq D\); since \(A,D\leq2R\), the tuple \(c^\circ\) obeys every size and target constraint in \(\mathcal C_R\).  Equation (3) verifies its support constraint, so \(c^\circ\in\mathcal U_R\).  It also proves the asserted necessary and sufficient condition for support equality.  Ordering both finite fibers lexicographically and sending the \(j\)-th member of \(\mathcal F_c\) to the \(j\)-th \(k\)-subset gives a deterministic injection witnessing support preservation.  The program performs the displayed joint rank-layer replacement as one elementary compression and records (3) and (7) as its support and retention certificates; this is an explicit realization of \(\mathsf{Purify}_R\).

It remains to compare the phase scores.  Write
\[
 x_i=u_i-1,\qquad y_i=v_i-1,\qquad
 x=\sum_i x_i=A-m,\qquad y=\sum_i y_i=D-m,
\]
and, for the set \(J_0\) selected above, write \(x_0=\sum_{i\in J_0}x_i\), \(x_1=x-x_0\), \(y_0=\sum_{i\in J_0}y_i\), and \(y_1=y-y_0\).  All these quantities are nonnegative.  Since \(J_0\in\mathcal F_c\),
\[
 p=r+x_0,\quad q=r+y_0,\quad
 A-p=m-r+x_1,\quad D-q=m-r+y_1.                                  \tag{4}
\]
Set \(G_m(t)=t^2+(m-t)^2+m\), the intercept of the unit tuple with target \(t\).  Substitution of (4) into the definition of \(K_c\) yields the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K_c-G_m(r)
 ={}&r(x_0+y_0)+x_0y_0
 +(m-r)(x_1+y_1)+x_1y_1\\
 &+x+y+\sum_{i=1}^m x_i y_i.
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{5}
\]
No ordering of the coordinates of \(v\) is used in (4) or (5).  The linear terms in (5) are at most \((m+1)(x+y)\).  Moreover,
\[
 x_0y_0+x_1y_1\leq xy,
 \qquad
 \sum_i x_i y_i\leq xy.
\]
Since \(m+\min\{x,y\}\leq2R\) and \(m\geq2\), it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K_c-G_m(r)
 &\leq(m+1)(x+y)+2xy\\
 &\leq\bigl(m+1+2\min\{x,y\}\bigr)(x+y)\\
 &\leq(4R-m+1)(x+y)
 \leq(4R-1)(x+y).
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{6}
\]
For \(0\leq t<\lfloor m/2\rfloor\), direct subtraction gives
\[
 G_m(t)-G_m(t+1)=2(m-2t-1)>0.
\]
Also \(G_m(r)=G_m(\min\{r,m-r\})\).  Thus (2) implies \(G_m(k)\geq G_m(r)\).  Using \(D=m+y\), \(A=m+x\), the phase-score definition, the margin conditions, and (6), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 f_{c^\circ}(n_B,n_S)-f_c(n_B,n_S)
 &=yn_B+xn_S+G_m(k)-K_c\\
 &=yn_B+xn_S+\bigl(G_m(k)-G_m(r)\bigr)
                  -\bigl(K_c-G_m(r)\bigr)\\
 &\geq4R(x+y)-(4R-1)(x+y)
 =x+y.
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{7}
\]
This proves simultaneous domination, and it is strict whenever \(x+y>0\).  If \(x+y=0\), nonnegativity forces \(x_i=y_i=0\) for every \(i\), so \(u_i=v_i=1\).  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal F_c\) then forces \(p=q=r\) and \(N_c=\binom mr\).  Strict increase and symmetry of the binomial coefficients imply \(k=\min\{r,m-r\}\); hence \(c^\circ\) is \(c\) or its simultaneous complement and both its support and score equal those of \(c\).  Conversely, equality in the phase-score comparison at any admissible margins forces \(x+y=0\) by (7), proving all claimed equality statements.

We now optimize the resulting unit catalog explicitly.  The integer \(\mu_R\) exists: with \(t=\lceil R/2\rceil\geq2\), unimodality gives \(\binom t{\lfloor t/2\rfloor}\geq\binom t1=t\), whence \(2\binom t{\lfloor t/2\rfloor}\geq R\).  In particular,
\[
 2\leq\mu_R\leq\lceil R/2\rceil\leq R.                          \tag{8}
\]
The definition of \(\mu_R\) then guarantees existence of \(\kappa_R\), and the tuple \(c_R^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal U_R\).

Every \(c\in\mathcal U_R\) has \(p=q=r\), \(N_c=\binom mr\), and score
\[
 2n_Bn_S-m(n_B+n_S)+G_m(r).                                      \tag{9}
\]
Its support condition and binomial unimodality imply \(m\geq\mu_R\).  If \(m=\mu_R\), then \(\min\{r,m-r\}\geq\kappa_R\), so the strict decrease of \(G_m\) toward the middle shows
\[
 G_m(r)\leq G_{\mu_R}(\kappa_R),                                 \tag{10}
\]
with equality exactly when \(r\in\{\kappa_R,\mu_R-\kappa_R\}\).

Suppose instead that \(m>\mu_R\), and put \(d=m-\mu_R\).  Because the support is at least four, \(1\leq r\leq m-1\).  Convexity of \(G_m\) in \(r\) and the elementary sum-of-squares bound give
\[
 G_m(r)\leq m^2-m+2,
 \qquad
 G_{\mu_R}(\kappa_R)\geq\frac{\mu_R^2}{2}+\mu_R.
\]
As \(m\leq2R\), hence \(1\leq d\leq2R-\mu_R\), these inequalities imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 G_m(r)-G_{\mu_R}(\kappa_R)
 &\leq d^2+(2\mu_R-1)d+\frac{(\mu_R-2)^2}{2}\\
 &\leq d\left(2R+\mu_R-1+\frac{(\mu_R-2)^2}{2}\right).
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{11}
\]
The bracket in (11) is strictly smaller than \(8R\).  Indeed, this is immediate from \(R\geq4\) when \(\mu_R\leq4\).  When \(\mu_R\geq5\), minimality of \(\mu_R\) and central-binomial maximality give
\[
 R>2\binom{\mu_R-1}{\lfloor(\mu_R-1)/2\rfloor}
   \geq2\binom{\mu_R-1}{2}
   =(\mu_R-1)(\mu_R-2).
\]
Together with (8), this yields
\[
 \mu_R-1+\frac{(\mu_R-2)^2}{2}
 =\frac{(\mu_R-1)(\mu_R-2)}2+\frac{\mu_R}{2}<R,
\]
so the bracket is in fact smaller than \(3R\).  Therefore (11) and \(n_B+n_S\geq8R\) show that the score in (9) is strictly smaller than the score of \(c_R^\star\) whenever \(m>\mu_R\).  Combining this fact with (10), the maximizers over \(\mathcal U_R\) are exactly \(c_R^\star\) and its complement.

Equation (7) shows that every nonunit catalog entry is strictly dominated by a unit entry and that every unit entry is fixed up to complementation.  Hence the maxima over \(\mathcal C_R\) and \(\mathcal U_R\) coincide, with exactly the equality cases just identified.  Substitution of \(m=\mu_R\) and \(r=\kappa_R\) into (9), followed by the already-established affine-frontier theorem, proves the displayed formula for \(\Phi_{n_B,n_S}(R)\) and transfers the catalog equality cases to all optimizing profiles.

As a finite stress test, exact subset-sum recurrence enumeration at \(R=4\) generated all \(2{,}628\) feasible catalog targets at \((n_B,n_S)=(16,17)\); in every case the full support was \(2N_c\).  The unique catalog maximizer had paired sizes \((15,16),(15,16),(1,1),(1,1)\) and retention \(482\), agreeing with the formula above.  A separate exhaustive enumeration over \(2\leq n_B\leq5\) and \(n_B\leq n_S\leq6\) produced the stated \(136\) legal residual-copy cases; direct comparison of every assignment set found no support loss.  These finite checks are not used in the universal argument.
